history.sg_progress: The Administration’s initial comments were reflected in paragraph 233 of the Board’s report, and additional comments from relevant entities are provided below. The Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs is actively working with the Finance Division in the Department of Management Strategy, Policy and Compliance on the capitalization of the intangible assets identified by the Board. The Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs is also working to ensure that internally developed (and off-the-shelf intangible assets) are identified and capitalized in a timely manner. The enhanced user guidance is being developed. In May 2024, the United Nations Office at Nairobi completed the recognition of its Division of Conference Services cost calculator application as an internally generated intangible asset. The Office will implement a more robust internal control of the review of its applications. The Office is also updating the standard operating procedure for its own intangible assets and those of its clients, which are expected to be reissued in the fourth quarter of 2024. The Department for General Assembly and Conference Management notes that it set up all technology projects with a software development component using the cost object in Umoja, and their cost is reported annually. Intangible assets are capitalized in line with International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) guidance. The Department will continue to work with the Division of Conference Services in Nairobi to apply the same principle for software development and that capitalization of assets that meet the threshold.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that relevant departments/offices enhance user access, guidance materials and monitoring mechanisms to improve the timeliness of intangible asset capitalization to ensure that expenditure is appropriately classified and recorded in Umoja in the future.
history.administration_response: The Administration requests that this recommendation be closed. Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs: Following instructions from and with the assistance of the Office of Programme Planning, Finance and Budget, the Department capitalized three internally developed intangible assets in 2024, including the two applications identified in the previous audit. Office of Programme Planning, Finance and Budget: The Office has further enhanced its year-end instructions and presentation to enforce more prudent management of intangible asset development projects and to emphasize the need for entities to capitalize intangible assets, including internally developed intangible assets. For 2024, entities will be required to provide an overview of all ongoing intangible asset development projects with expected completion dates and will receive additional guidance on the completion or termination of intangible asset projects. Furthermore, the Office has updated the Umoja user access guide to clarify who can obtain access to the Umoja roles needed for the capitalization of intangible assets. United Nations Office at Nairobi: In May 2024, the Office completed the recognition of the cost calculator application of the Division for Conference Services in Nairobi as an internally generated intangible asset. The Office has updated the standard operating procedure for its intangible assets and its clients and launched the standard operating procedure during the closure of the 2024 accounts. Department for General Assembly and Conference Management: In close coordination with the Department of Management Strategy, Policy and Compliance, the Department for General Assembly and Conference Management has simplified and streamlined financial accounting to capture project costs. Given that the Office of Programme Planning, Finance and Budget agreed to record regular budget post funding in Umoja at the project level, effective 1 January 2025, all project costs, including position costs (regular budget and extrabudgetary), have been captured in Umoja at the work breakdown structure element (individual project account) level. In the first quarter of 2025, the Department for General Assembly and Conference Management closely monitored Umoja transactions and adapted to changes in funding sources, given the challenging liquidity environment. With the improved reporting capabilities, the Department for General Assembly and Conference Management is able to accurately report project costs on a monthly basis and to release additional budgets based on the progress made.
history.board_assessment: Given that the Administration has taken a series of measures to deal with this issue, the Board considers the recommendation to be implemented.
